slot.brief: Two/three concurrent forces in equilibrium with one unknown force magnitude or angle; resolve into components and solve.

stem: Two forces of $3$ N east and $4$ N north act concurrently on a particle. A third force balances them and makes an angle $\theta$ south of west. What is $\theta$?

verdicts.working: The balancing force has components 3 N west and 4 N south, so \(\tan\theta=4/3\) and \(\theta=53.1^\circ\).

working:
For equilibrium, the third force has components $(-3,-4)$ N.\\
$\tan\theta=\dfrac{4}{3}$\\
$\theta=53.1^\circ$

Independent check: The balancing force has components 3 N west and 4 N south, so \(\tan\theta=4/3\) and \(\theta=53.1^\circ\).
solution:
For equilibrium, the third force has components $(-3,-4)$ N.
$$\tan\theta=\frac{4}{3}\quad\Rightarrow\quad \theta=53.1^\circ$$
